researchHistory.summary: Targeted Alicante re-research using municipal heritage/housing/planning sources, Port Authority, MARQ, Mercalicante and official tourism sources. notes: Refinement: the generic open-block slab family remains shared, but Virgen del Remedio and Ciudad Elegida Juan XXIII now have documented city-specific subprofiles rather than one interchangeable northern-estate appearance.
Planning guardrail: Nueva Albufereta four-by-ten-storey information and PAU 5 Sector 2 dwelling counts remain future/transition evidence and are not promoted to current built form.

Refinement: Alicante port morphology requires a city-facing Levante passenger/leisure grammar distinct from Poniente operational/logistics grammar; cruise-terminal scale is directly supported by the Port Authority.
Semantic normalization: Mercalicante is retained under its stable building ID but treated as a multi-building logistics/wholesale complex rather than a fictitious single object.
Refinement: Nueva Tabarca traditional houses are split from broad mainland historic/peripheral families and remain a city-specific profile under a shared attached-house structural archetype.

New visual/game anchors: Explanada de España, Postiguet, Casa Carbonell, Lonja del Pescado and Torre de San José are added because they materially improve waterfront/island identity rather than merely increasing POI count.
Topographic identity: Santa Bárbara and San Fernando now carry explicit evidence that their built form is inseparable from Benacantil/Tossal relief.
